title: Blue Hour Stroll
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand walks the bass in steady quarter notes through the chord tones. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: Blue Hour Stroll is a complete jazz piano song in C major, in 4/4 time at 132 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: walking bass in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Swinging on the Rooftop
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: Swinging on the Rooftop is a complete jazz piano song in F major, in 4/4 time at 176 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Bebop Alley Run
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: The Bebop Alley Run is a complete jazz piano song in Eb major, in 4/4 time at 64 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Slow Smoke Ballad
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. Shape the phrasing in two-bar breaths and let the syncopation sit inside the beat, never ahead of it.
body: Slow Smoke Ballad is a complete jazz piano song in A major, in 4/4 time at 176 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Uptown Swing Set
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand walks the bass in steady quarter notes through the chord tones. Shape the phrasing in two-bar breaths and let the syncopation sit inside the beat, never ahead of it.
body: The Uptown Swing Set is a complete jazz piano song in E major, in 4/4 time at 96 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: walking bass in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Stride and Sway
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. Shape the phrasing in two-bar breaths and let the syncopation sit inside the beat, never ahead of it.
body: Stride and Sway is a complete jazz piano song in F major, in 4/4 time at 176 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Bebop in the Back Room
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand walks the bass in steady quarter notes through the chord tones. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: Bebop in the Back Room is a complete jazz piano song in D major, in 4/4 time at 96 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: walking bass in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Velvet Hour Ballad
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand walks the bass in steady quarter notes through the chord tones. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: The Velvet Hour Ballad is a complete jazz piano song in Bb major, in 4/4 time at 132 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: walking bass in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Swing Set for a Sunday Afternoon
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: Swing Set for a Sunday Afternoon is a complete jazz piano song in Eb major, in 4/4 time at 64 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Blue Note Walk
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: The Blue Note Walk is a complete jazz piano song in A major, in 4/4 time at 176 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through twelve-bar blues roots in eight-bar sections, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Closing Set at the Jazz Cellar
era: Jazz era, public swing, bebop, ballad, stride and blues frameworks
technique: Left hand walks the bass in steady quarter notes through the chord tones. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: Closing Set at the Jazz Cellar is a complete jazz piano song in E major, in 4/4 time at 96 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original genre study in the public musical language of jazz: swing feel, bebop-style lines, ballad phrasing, stride bass and blues-based forms. It is explicitly not any existing copyrighted jazz song, and no existing standard's melody is used. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: walking bass in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.
